title: the same operation gets the same verdict, and a refusal says what to do
description: Tasks: (1) A verdict table (operation class x tier) that the hook corpus asserts; the operator decides three undefined boundary cases. (2) Shell-write refusal text names what to do (the file is outside the running task; scope it or ask) instead of 'use the Edit/Write tools'. (3) The orchestrator recognizes the auto-mode classifier's no-verdict text and records could-not-run. (4) Only after measuring the 3.0.x refusals: the same verdict for Edit and a shell write of the same change - guard-reading code, written by the human maintainer.
desiredOutcome: for every documented operation class the plan gate's verdict is written down per tier, a refusal never tells the model to use a tool the harness steers away from, and a classifier that gives no verdict is recorded as could-not-run, not as a failed attempt

tasks.title: Assert the plan gate's verdict per operation class and tier from the hook corpus
tasks.description: Write the plan gate's verdict contract as a test: a table keyed by operation class, each class naming its verdict at observe, warn and deny. Its instances are the hook corpus rows handed over in the brief, cited by row id. Each row goes through py-launch.sh to every PreToolUse hook hooks.json registers for its tool, against three fixture projects built under _harness.fixture_root with a local git identity, since the sweep supplies none. Rows whose current verdict differs from their class's intent are marked known-divergence with the basis they contradict, so the human task flips them rather than the table hiding them. Today those are b02, b03o and b17s, refused through the shell where the same change passes through Edit. Before spawning, the orchestrator asks the operator for the verdict of the three rows no document defines (b06, b10, g06) and passes the answers in. An answer that differs from today's behaviour is filed with /audit:bug and its row marked known-divergence. The documented-gap rows stay out of this table; they belong to the phase that names open shapes in SECURITY.md. The file is new, but _output.selftest_coverage() already assigns this name to hooks/hooks.json, so it is not an orphan and needs no layer, guide section or preamble. Measure its wall clock twice with a gap and report the spread.

tasks.title: Make shell-write refusals name the remedy instead of the Edit/Write tools
tasks.description: The deny and ask texts of guard-secrets-read's shell-write arms tell the model to use the Edit/Write tools, and guard-bash-writes' notices say the same. That is the opposite of what the harness tells a model in auto mode. Reword each to say what is true and what to do: the file is outside the running task (name the phase), so widen the task with /audit:task scope <taskId> --files <path>, or stop and ask the operator; exempt paths are unaffected. Only message constants and docstrings change, never grading logic. That includes the docstring sentences in guard-secrets-read.py and _config.plan_gate_mode that claim one file gets one verdict however it is written: they must name the first-trivial-file allowance as Edit-only until the verdict task lands. Update the existing case that pins the old phrase.

tasks.title: Record a classifier no-verdict as could-not-run, not as a failed attempt
tasks.description: When the auto-mode permission classifier cannot reach a verdict, Claude Code refuses the tool call with text containing 'auto mode cannot determine the safety' or 'gave no verdict' (the wording seen in 2.1.2xx transcripts). The pipeline reads that as a failed attempt. Add an arm beside the infrastructure arm in execute-task.md: that text means the step produced no verdict. The arm records could-not-run with the refusal verbatim in task.outcome.technical, reverts the attempts increment, leaves the task in_progress, and reports the classifier as unavailable rather than raising a human fix item. Add the matching progress line to orchestrator.md, and tell the executor in audit-executor.md to report such a refusal verbatim as could-not-run, never as fail. Pin the fragments and their routing in test__refs.py so the rule has a mechanism. Blocked by P100, which edits both reference files.

add: plugins/audit/tests/test__refs.py: execute-task.md carries the classifier no-verdict fragments in an arm that records could-not-run with the refusal verbatim, reverts the attempts increment and raises no human fix item
plugins/audit/tests/test__refs.py: audit-executor.md tells the executor to report a tool call refused with that text as could-not-run with the refusal verbatim, never as fail

tasks.title: Give a shell write the same plan-gate verdict as Edit of the same change
tasks.description: Make a shell write and Edit of the same change get the same plan-gate verdict. The shell-write arm of guard-secrets-read reads the session's first-trivial-file slot the way require-plan does, through one reader moved into _config so the two cannot drift. The human decides how a shell write's magnitude is measured when the command does not state it, and once the verdicts agree, restores the one-verdict docstring sentences the message task qualified. Precondition, without which this task does not start: sort the shell-write refusals recorded since 3.0.0 into covered, first-trivial and uncovered, and record the result on this task with /audit:task note together with the command that produced it. An executor attempts the guard-reading code first, because the maintainer wants code written by agents; Claude also supplies the tests and the corpus rows. This step may be stopped by the model's safeguard; if so, record the refusal verbatim and hand it to the human.
